newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says policies not based on polls.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says policies not based on polls.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said his policies were designed to obtain results in the long- term and were not guided by his falling position in the polls, Peruvian television reported Tuesday.

"We have not worked for immediate results for the sake of popularity polls. The measures we have taken are so that we can have a country with a long-term vision," Fujimori told Peruvian reporters, who were travelling with him in Thailand on the third leg of a four-country Southeast Asia tour.

According to leading Peruvian pollster, Apoyo, Fujimori's public approval rating dipped to 52 percent at the end of October, from 55 percent at the beginning of the month. Earlier this week, other pollsters said they believed the president's rating had now fallen below 50 percent.

Fujimori, who took office in 1990 and won re-election last year with an overwhelming 64 percent of the vote, has held relatively high popularity ratings during his term due mainly to the virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reforms and strong, personalized leadership style.

But the administration's failure to reduce high levels of poverty and unemployment, Fujimori's perceived authoritarianism, his possible bid for a third term, and the influence of his shadowy security adviser Vladimiro Montesinos, are starting to take a toll on the president's popularity, analysts say.

Congress recently approved an interpretation of the constitution that would allow Fujimori to run for the presidency again in 2000. But opposition legislators, backed by large sections of the population, are campaigning for a referendum on the issue.
Fujimori has already taken in Japan and the Philippines on his Asian tour aimed at promoting investment in Peru. He is also set to visit Malaysia before returning to Peru on November 22.
